# The Equifax Credit Report: Providing a Fuller Financial Picture for Every Mortgage Decision


October 12, 2026


When a consumer submits a mortgage application, every data point matters. That makes the breadth of data behind each credit report critical — and it's where Equifax credit report differentiators matter, including the company’s ability to provide alternative data and employment insights alongside the traditional mortgage credit file to create a fuller financial picture of a borrower. This fuller picture can help make mortgage underwriting faster and easier.


#### More Data at No Additional Cost to Lenders


For many consumers, paying phone, cable, and electric bills on time is a core part of their financial life. Yet those payments often don't appear in traditional credit files.


Equifax is the only Nationwide Consumer Reporting Agency to provide[alternative data](https://www.equifax.com/business/blog/-/insight/article/leveling-up-how-alternative-data-reveals-deeper-customer-insights/) — Fair Credit Reporting Act-complaint information not typically included in a traditional credit report such as utility and telecommunications payment histories — alongside consumer credit reports for the mortgage market, at no additional cost to lenders.


While traditional credit reports remain a strong indicator of credit history and past financial reliability, alternative data can responsibly expand access to credit and support a more inclusive economy. Including alternative data insights allows consumers to get the full benefits of their history of responsible and on-time payments. By including these insights alongside the credit report, Equifax helps more consumers qualify for automated underwriting — streamlining the underwriting process with information that can only be used to help consumers obtain a mortgage loan.


#### Employment Insights, Earlier in the Mortgage Process


Equifax empowers lenders with two innovative solutions that deliver income and employment insights earlier on in the mortgage process:


-


[Income Qualify](https://www.equifax.com/business/product/income-qualify/) delivers income and employment insights from The Work Number® to mortgage lenders during the prequalification and pre-approval phase, at no additional cost, alongside the Equifax consumer credit file. Having front-end access to this critical information can reduce the need for borrowers to provide documentation of their income and employment, while improving mortgage processing efficiency by minimizing manual errors, delays, and reducing risk in the lending process while supporting affordability in the home buying process.


-


[The Work Number® Report Indicator](https://www.equifax.com/business/product/the-work-number-report-indicator/) , also delivered alongside the Equifax consumer credit file, simplifies the mortgage application experience for borrowers and speeds up loan processing by enabling lenders to instantly see whether an applicant has a standard verification of income and employment (VOI/E) record on The Work Number database. That early visibility makes the lending process easier for lenders and applicants alike.


#### Accuracy Lenders Can Count On


Equifax is always working to make its credit reports as accurate and reliable as possible. When it comes to credit report accuracy, the organization believes even one error is one too many. Equifax is committed to improving its data processes and transparently reports its accuracy metrics on a monthly basis. For September 2026, Equifax U.S. consumer credit report accuracy was 99.83%*.


The Equifax U.S. consumer credit file maintains more than 3.6 billion credit accounts with over 1.6 billion updates monthly to currently reported accounts. As part of its commitment to accuracy, Equifax continuously monitors and enhances its processes to improve data quality in consumer credit files and making it easier for consumers to access their Equifax credit report and correct any potential errors quickly.


Equifax is also working with data furnishers to enhance the accuracy of the information reported. And, as part of its approximately $3 billion investment in the[Equifax Cloud](https://www.equifax.com/about-equifax/equifax-cloud/) ™, the organization is continually developing new programs that will enable it to identify potential accuracy issues and correct them before a consumer disputes information on their credit report.


#### The Bottom Line for Consumers and Lenders


Equifax will continue to innovate and responsibly support its customers with the fullest insights available — helping more people move forward on the path to homeownership.


*The metric is determined by calculating the number of tradeline, collection, and bankruptcy disputes within the month that resulted in a change to a U.S. consumer credit report, regardless of whether that change had any impact on a consumer's credit score.
